REGULAR MEETING OF THE BOARD OF SUPERVISORS
  ORANGE COUNTY, CALIFORNIA

  Tuesday, October 22, 2024,9 : 0 0 A . M .

  BOARD HEARING ROOM, FIRST FLOOR
  400 W. Civic Center Drive
  Santa Ana, California

  DONALD P. WAGNER
  CHAIRMAN
  Third District

 DOUG CHAFFEE  ANDREW DO
 VICE CHAIRMAN  SUPERVISOR
 Fourth District  First District

 VICENTE SARMIENTO  KATRINA
 SUPERVISOR  FOLEY
 Second District  SUPERVISOR

ATTENDANCE:Supervisors: Chaffee, Foley, Sarmiento and Wagner

EXCUSED:Supervisor Do (Agenda Items 1-14)

 PRESENT:  INTERIM COUNTY EXECUTIVE  Michelle Aguirre

INVOCATION:Supervisor Foley, Fifth District, gave the invocation

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:Supervisor Sarmiento, Second District, led the assembly in the Pledge of
Allegiance

I.PRESENTATIONS/INTRODUCTIONS

 Week"

 Muertos"

 "National Breast Cancer Awareness Month"

VI.PUBLIC, CEO, ADJOURNMENT & BOARD COMMENTS

PUBLIC COMMENTS:

Lupe Morfin - Oral Re: Laws and rules have changed and people need to fight for rights and integrity
in voting; registration with Real ID should be required and only citizens should be allowed to vote;
requested to look at the inhumane conditions at the Registrar of Voters warehouses

Brigitte - Oral Re: Quoted Tupac Shakur; Trump is going to prove the election was stolen; document
and public comments provided at 5/24/22 Board meeting; treatment of seniors and desecration of his
mother; update regarding Klubnikin case; County Counsel violated subpoena rules and lawyers engage
in fraud

John W. Spring - Oral Re: Memories of his wife who passed in 2021; October 19th is America's real
independence day; sent analytical report to President John F. Kennedy regarding US Naval blockade of
Cuba; approached by agent of Defense Intelligence Agency in 1961

Elizabeth Rios - Oral Re: County should not allow Social Services Agency to seize children from
parents without a warrant; children were removed after disciplining her teenage daughter by taking her
cell phone away which is not abuse; hearing on October 29th and requested Board return her children
and investigate matter

Toni Taloa - Oral Re: Home care provider for her sister; In-Home Supportive Services (IHSS) wage
increases allowed purchase of daily essentials that she was unable to previously provide

Gloria - Oral Re: Home care provider for her mother; In-Home Supportive Services (IHSS) benefits
and wage increases for United Domestic Workers of America (UDW) are life changing; insurance
benefits helped her with her health condition and to continue caring for her mom

Alberta Martinez - Oral Re:In-Home Supportive Services (IHSS) provider for 10 years; lost her
husband and IHSS benefits helped cover funeral and other expenses during very difficult times
  Ilya Tsegin - Oral Re: Demands resignation of Chairman Wagner and revocation of his law license;
 Board misrepresents elected officials who are corrupted in Orange County such as judges and County
 officials; suppressing constitutional free speech

 Nick Kolev - Oral Re: Reported felony committed by Carlotta Serna, Chief Legal Counsel for Child
 Support Services who says he owes child support money to the State disbursement unit; passport
 renewal is blocked

 Cheryl - Oral Re: Problems with voter rolls in primary election; voter rolls are not accurate as required
 by the National Voter Registration Act of 1993; Supervisor Sarmiento's absence from public
 comments; had no intentions of disparaging Supervisor's son

 Kate - Oral Re: 2021 recall, 2022 election and the 2024 primary were fraudulent; could save money
 and be better if the Board of Supervisors were closed down, removed County Executive Officer and
 County Counsels salaries and bomb building (CAN); Board needs to take care of the fundamental right
 provided by the almighty GOD in the Constitution of the United States, right to vote and select
 representatives from cities to the federal government; need to clean voter rolls

 Roseann - Oral Re: Democracy is majority rule system and clarifying we are not a democracy, we are a
 constitutional republic; Board has the responsibility not to certify elections that violate the law;
 certification of the 2024 election; cease and desist letter regarding certification of election; nothing has
 been done to cleanup voter rolls; voting system needs to be auditable; need back-up voting system for
 power outages

 Lisa H - Oral Re: Volunteers for the United Sovereign Americans (USA) read into the public record

 2022 election indicates it was invalid and Shirley Webber served with complaint

 Eileen McDermott - Oral Re: Provided information for informed voters in 2024; quit shutting the
 public from speaking and listen; names of prominent people in government who are married to
 prominent people in the media which proves they are all connected and it is all rigged; Kamala Harris'
 husband was Executive at DLA Piper and in charge of Clinton Foundation audit

 Bryan Kaye - Oral Re: Board interaction with public during Board meetings; additional speaker time
 provided to one speaker; freedom of speech and silencing the public

 Mary - Oral Re: Waste of money sending election materials in the mail; people can register to vote
 without ID and without any kind of verification, voter rolls are inaccurate, votes can be changed
 electronically on uncertified equipment; no audit control and rules are not followed; provided list of
 items not required by hand counting of ballots

COUNTY EXECUTIVE OFFICER COMMENTS:
 None

ADJOURNED:12.50 P.M.
 5324  Adjourned in memory of Buzz Amble

BOARD COMMENTS:

 Supervisor Foley - Oral Re: Provided comments regarding the indictment, guilty plea and resignation
 of Andrew Do from the Orange County Board of Supervisors; disgusted by the level of corruption in
   the indictment and the allegations of bribery; County will continue to investigate any further actions
  coming out of District 1 and the Board as a whole is committed to implementing reforms and protocols
  that will prevent this from happening again

  Supervisor Sarmiento - Oral Re: Investigation of Andrew Do and misuse of public funds in a bribery
  scheme where he directed taxpayer dollars to organizations and payments to himself and his family and
  exploiting the people he purported to champion; plea agreement and resignation; the Board should look
  at how to better ensure disclosure, transparency and more open government; thanked journalist Nick
  Gerda and media for making sure Board was alerted of misconduct
